supporting_observations.claim: At 13:45:43 UTC, FILE-COP-01 sent 640,000,259 bytes to PROXY-COP-01 on port 8080; the record shows a large transfer to the proxy, not the ultimate external destination.
The transfer size is compatible with the inventory description of Ironvault uploads, but this record does not identify Ironvault, the initiating process, or the ultimate destination.

An RDP connection from WS-SALI-01, where sara.ali launched mstsc, to FILE-COP-01 began at 13:39:45 UTC and lasted about 31 minutes, overlapping the transfer. The evidence does not link that session to the transfer.

known_telemetry_limitations: FILE-COP-01 winsec and sysmon collection was unavailable from 13:25 to 14:15 UTC, including the transfer period, so the initiating process and relevant host activity cannot be verified.
PROXY-COP-01 proxy-log collection was unavailable from 13:25 to 14:15 UTC, so the proxy request’s destination, URL, and associated identity are not available.
Zeek connection data records the transfer to the explicit proxy, but the provided records do not establish what data was sent or whether it reached an approved backup service.
claims_not_established: That the transfer was made by the Ironvault agent or was an authorized backup.
That the transfer reached ironvault-cloud.com or any other specific external destination.
What files or data were transferred, or whether the transfer was authorized.
Whether sara.ali's overlapping RDP session caused, enabled, or was unrelated to the transfer.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover PROXY-COP-01 access logs or equivalent upstream records for the transfer, including destination, URL, request identity, and byte counts.
Obtain FILE-COP-01 Ironvault agent logs, backup job records, and any transfer manifests for the alerted time.
Restore or collect host execution and file-access telemetry for FILE-COP-01 covering the outage window.
Review the sara.ali RDP session and determine whether it had a connection to the transfer.
unrelated_findings: A Kerberos service-ticket event for svc-backup on FILE-COP-01 records a client address of 116.202.120.181 shortly before the transfer. Given the stated lack of VPN, investigate this separately; the available evidence does not connect it to the alerted transfer. (T110-00290)

The overlapping RDP session originated from the help-desk workstation, although the inventory says remote administration is only done from WS-PBECKER-01. Investigate the session separately; the evidence does not establish that it caused the transfer. (T110-00199, T110-00207, T110-00209)
